metadata.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock II

problem_summary.summary: Maximize profit across as many non-overlapping stock transactions as desired, holding at most one share at a time.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: daily prices. Return the maximum total profit from buying before selling; multiple transactions are permitted.

brute_force.explanation: Explore every legal choice each day: when not holding, either wait or buy; when holding, either wait or sell. Reject paths that finish while still holding.
brute_force.correctness_idea: Every valid trading schedule is a sequence of these daily choices, so exhaustive branching includes an optimal schedule.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(2^n) worst case — each day can branch into waiting or changing the holding state.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(n) recursion stack — the decision path can span all days.

optimized.explanation: Add every positive day-to-day price increase. This captures each rising run's full gain without needing to locate the run's endpoints explicitly.
optimized.correctness_idea: For any consecutive rising prices, summing adjacent increases telescopes to the gain from the run's low to high. Falling steps cannot improve profit, so retaining only positive differences is optimal.
optimized.time_complexity: O(n) — each adjacent pair is checked once.
optimized.space_complexity: O(1) auxiliary — only the running profit is stored.

steps.action: Add the positive rise 3 to profit.
Add the positive rise 3 and return total profit 9.

edge_cases.case: Prices only decrease or stay level
edge_cases.handling: No positive difference is added, so profit is zero.
All adjacent gains sum to the total first-to-last increase.
There are no adjacent pairs and the result is zero.
